title: Hana, Maui County Water Dept. of Water Supply Conservation Plan Community Meeting: January 25, 2024

issues.title: Using recycled R1 water for irrigation and firefighting

recap.headline: Water Supply seeks Hāna feedback on countywide water conservation plan
recap.in_60_seconds: The County Department of Water Supply and its consultant, Carollo Engineers, held a virtual community meeting focused on the Hāna-area water systems to get feedback on a new Water Shortage and Conservation Plan. Staff proposed a goal of cutting per-person water use 10 percent in Hāna and Molokaʻi and 20 percent in Central, West Maui and Upcountry by 2040, using about 20 measures such as smart meters, a three-day-a-week irrigation limit and a water waste ordinance. Four residents spoke, and a short online poll ranked smart meters (Ami) first, followed by a hotel and resort program. Residents raised fairness about hotel water use, how mandates apply to catchment users, confusing drought-restriction messaging, and poor awareness of the free toilet program. Staff said the plan should be done by the end of March, but gave no date for smart meters in Hāna and did not clearly answer how Haʻikū's grouping with Upcountry affects its restrictions.

parts.title: Welcome and purpose
parts.presenter: Department of Water Supply water resources planner
presented: First virtual meeting in a series seeking feedback on proposed conservation measures for all districts, focused on Hāna

parts.title: Background on the County conservation program and goals
parts.presenter: Department of Water Supply water resources planner
presented: The Department serves Hāna town and Hāmoa, plus separate systems at Keʻanae, Nāhiku and Kaupō; it does not serve Kīpahulu.
Water use per meter has dropped about 25 percent over 25 years; free low-flow fixtures save about 300,000 gallons a day.
Hāna uses about 0.4 million gallons a day at 143 gallons per person per day, versus 249 countywide and 291 in Central Maui.

Proposed goal: 20 percent cut for large systems and 10 percent for Hāna and Molokaʻi, bringing Hāna from 143 to 130 gallons per person per day by 2040 and saving about 11 million gallons a day countywide.

next.what: Water Shortage and Conservation Plan completed

parts.title: Proposed conservation measures
presented: About 150 possible measures were screened down to about 20 for Maui.
Smart meters with the EyeOnWater app, with most meters replaced in the next two to three years.
Proposed ordinances limiting lawn watering to no more than three days a week, banning water waste, and requiring efficient fixtures in new development.
Rebates, a hotel and resort audit program, low-income plumbing help, a review of tiered water rates, and pre-rinse spray valves that can save 16,000 gallons each.

parts.title: Online priority poll
presented: Five people responded; smart meters (Ami) led, followed by the hotel and resort program.
Department staff said smart meters and education and outreach also ranked high at earlier meetings.

parts.title: Questions and talk story
parts.presenter: Department of Water Supply water resources planner

raised.concern: Little in the plan on emergency planning for fires or keeping reservoirs filled.
Haʻikū and the North Shore are grouped with Upcountry even though conditions there are wetter and more like Hāna.
Residents are asked to conserve while hotels are the biggest users; the County should work with large users as Oʻahu has.
Whether water losses have been analyzed for each system to prioritize fixes on the County side.
Whether the effort should focus on the highest-use districts since Hāna savings are very small.
How watering mandates would work for households on catchment or private wells.
Drought-restriction messaging and the website are confusing, for example on whether power washing is allowed.
Whether there are incentives or programs for reusing water.

answered.who: Department of Water Supply water resources planner
answered.said: The plan includes a section setting triggers for declaring a water shortage and short-term actions during drought; reservoirs and new supply are long-term actions.

answered.who: Department of Water Supply water resources planner
answered.said: Staff recently analyzed water use per room at low- to high-end resorts in South and West Maui to target audits.

answered.who: Department of Water Supply water resources planner
answered.said: The 20 percent goal applies only to the larger systems with more growth; Hāna and Molokaʻi have a 10 percent goal, though measures apply countywide and some to private systems.
This project does not analyze water losses in depth; Hāna appears to have somewhat higher non-revenue water, and the plan recommends system-specific water audits.
The County is developing hydraulic models and an asset management program that will help with planning.

answered.who: Department of Water Supply water resources planner
answered.said: Mandates cannot apply to small household catchment or private well systems; incentives to conserve still apply.

answered.who: Department of Water Supply water resources planner
answered.said: The Department has heard at all three meetings that its messaging is poor; Haʻikū can face real shortages even in rain when its well is down.

answered.who: Department of Water Supply water resources planner
answered.said: Reclaimed water is run by the Department of Environmental Management; Water Supply is piloting gray water, including spray irrigation at Kanahā Beach Park, and studying desalination.

parts.title: Discussion of conservation goals and outreach
parts.presenter: Department of Water Supply water resources planner
presented: Staff asked whether the 20 percent goal is too aggressive or not enough and said it must fit limited funds and staff.

raised.concern: Whether the Department has reached out to the Oʻahu Board of Water Supply given its success.
Few people know about the free toilet program; suggested repeated social media promotion.

answered.who: Department of Water Supply water resources planner
answered.said: She talks often with her counterpart at the Oʻahu Board of Water Supply and learns from that agency.
About 40 toilets remain; the program has been promoted on radio, the website and flyers, but word of mouth works best.

answered.who: Department of Water Supply water resources planner
answered.said: Suggestions on better community outreach are always welcome because it is a chronic challenge.

parts.title: Closing
parts.presenter: Department of Water Supply water resources planner
presented: Follow-up questions and comments can be sent through contact information on the County website.

next.what: Send follow-up comments to the Department of Water Supply

bills.name: Maui Island Water Use and Development Plan
bills.what: Long-range water plan approved in 2022 that adopted conservation goals and preferred measures.

bills.name: Water Shortage and Conservation Plan
bills.what: Plan being developed to set water shortage triggers and conservation measures and goals for each district.

bills.name: Proposed irrigation schedule ordinance
bills.what: Would limit lawn watering to no more than three days a week and bar daytime watering.

bills.name: Proposed water waste ordinance
bills.what: Would define and prohibit water waste, such as unrepaired leaks and watering after rain.

open_questions.question: How does grouping Haʻikū with the Upcountry system affect its drought restrictions, and is power washing allowed during them?
When will smart meters be installed in the Hāna-area systems?
How much water is lost in each Hāna-area system and what will be done about it?

not_on_tracker.topic: Hotel and resort water use versus residents' conservation
not_on_tracker.why: Residents feel they are asked to cut back while large resorts use the most water.

not_on_tracker.topic: Smart meter rollout and the EyeOnWater app
not_on_tracker.why: It was the top priority in the poll and lets customers catch leaks and track use.

not_on_tracker.topic: Awareness of the free ultra-efficient toilet program
not_on_tracker.why: Residents said few people know about it, and only about 40 toilets remain.

moments.quote: And this plan is, we intend to have it completed by the end of March.
moments.about: Gives the department's target for finishing the countywide water shortage and conservation plan that Upcountry residents also commented on.

moments.quote: So if we set a pretty aggressive goal of 20% for the systems that have the larger demand and see most the growth, which would be the central upcountry in Lahaina, and for the smaller rural system, a 10% goal, these are really efficient what is already, we could bring that gallons per day per capita down from 249 to 200 gallons per capita per day. And we think it's possible with the right portfolio of conservation measures.
moments.about: Explains the proposed conservation targets in the plan, including a 20% goal for the Upcountry system.

moments.quote: Back to the way Haiku North Shore is grouped with upcountry. Like with this recent drought restrictions, my personal situation is my driveway desperately needs to be power washed.
moments.about: A Haʻikū resident describes how being grouped with the Upcountry system under drought restrictions affects them despite heavy local rain.

moments.quote: So, even in operational issues, we end up having a true shortage in Haiku, even during rain, because the well is down for various reasons for an extended time.
moments.about: Explains why Haʻikū faces water shortage restrictions even during rain, because its well has been down.
